Dentist in Houston
Get to Know Dr. Brad Jetton
Dr. Jetton started saying he wanted to become a dentist in high school. The more he pursued this goal, the more he enjoyed it. He not only discovered he liked doing the actual work of dentistry, the procedures themselves, but also developing relationships with his patients. For over 15 years, he says these connections have made his life better in countless ways, and his goal is to do the same for his patients in Houston every time they come to see him.
Where Did You Study Dentistry?
Born and raised in Wichita Falls, Dr. Brad Jetton earned his bachelor’s degree in biology from Midwestern State University and received his Doctor of Dental Surgery from the University of Texas Dental Branch (now called the UT Health Houston School of Dentistry). A proud general dentist able to provide a wide range of procedures to meet his patients’ needs, he also completed the American Academy of Implant Dentistry’s Maxicourse to offer the highest quality tooth replacement possible.
Outside of the Dental Office, What Do You Like to Do?
Dr. Jetton and his wife, Suzie, have a daughter, Sydney, as well as two dogs, Nolan and Dixie. When he’s not with family or taking care of patients, you’ll usually find him reading, playing guitar, or golfing (he’s a frequent volunteer at the Houston Open).

Preventive Dentistry Houston
The Best of the Basics
While Dr. Jetton can provide all types of dental services, some of the most effective are the ones you’re likely familiar with: checkups and cleanings. These and other preventive dentistry treatments in Houston help patients avoid the most common dental issues and catch them early if they pop up. They offer peace of mind while protecting your health, so reach out today to schedule your next appointment.
Why Choose New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston for Preventive Dentistry?
Trusted by Houston for Over 45 Years
Able to See the Entire Family
High-Quality & Budget-Friendly
What to Expect at Your Dental Appointment
Here is what we will do when you come in to make your experience as pleasant as possible:
We will partner with you to provide you with an oral health experience. Our approach to dentistry is centered around the philosophy that every mouth is unique and deserves special attention. Because of this, Dr. Jetton will collaborate with you so that you can make the best decision for your oral health together.
Education is an important part of every visit. We don’t just care for your teeth and send you on your way. We will also teach you how to care for your teeth and maintain a vibrant smile during all of your daily activities. Good oral hygiene habits are essential for maintaining a healthy smile.
We provide a comfortable and relaxing environment. Dentists make some people nervous. We understand that and take special care to make our office as comfortable as possible. Our patients are heard and treated with compassion. You are a member of our family, and we want you to feel at home with us.
We know that receiving quality service is a huge consideration when choosing which dentist to visit. We are here to help transform your smile because we want to make sure that you are getting the most out of your teeth every day.
Dental Checkups & Cleanings
While we’ll definitely keep an eye out for cavities during your checkup, we’ll also look for things like the early signs of oral cancer. That way, patients can get treatment quickly. With a professional cleaning, plaque and bacteria buildup from the hard-to-reach areas of your mouth is completely eliminated. As a bonus, this also takes care of minor surface stains to help your smile stay white!
Gum Disease Treatment
Are your gums easily irritated or swollen? Do they bleed when you brush and floss them? If your gums have been red or sensitive for a while, there is a good chance that you could be dealing with the early stages of gum disease, otherwise known as gingivitis. We can help you regain a happy and healthy smile with treatments like scaling and root planing and laser gum treatment.
Nightguards for Teeth Grinding (Bruxism)
Millions of people unconsciously grind their teeth while they sleep—are you one of them? Do you wake up with headaches, a sore jaw, or have teeth that look worn down? If so, we can provide you with a custom-made nightguard. This comfortable mouthpiece is only worn to bed and will protect your teeth, dental work, and jaw muscles while you rest.
TMJ Treatment
We can help patients dealing with issues that not only affect their teeth, but their jaw joint as well (known as the temporomandibular joint, or TMJ). Things like teeth grinding or an uneven bite can cause stiffness, pain, and headaches like migraines. Our team can identify the root cause of the discomfort, correct any imbalances, and create custom mouthguards that take the stress off of overworked and strained facial muscles.

Why Choose New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston for Replacing Missing Teeth?
45+ Years of Reliable Dentistry for Houston

Dental Bridges
This prosthetic literally bridges the gap left by one or more consecutive missing teeth. How? The new teeth are attached to crowns on either side, closing the space. Our bridges look natural, restore chewing strength, and prevent the remaining teeth from drifting out of place over time.
Dental Implants
Unlike other replacement options, dental implants bring back both the root and crown of a tooth. Small posts are placed into the jawbone that create a sturdy foundation for a crown, bridge, or denture. They look incredibly lifelike and can easily last for 25+ years.
Learn More About Dental Implants
Dentures
Today’s dentures are very customizable. Rather than giving you a one-size-fits-all solution, your prosthetic will be meticulously designed based on your unique anatomy, bite, and aesthetic goals. Whether you need a partial or full denture, we’ll make sure you’re able to speak, eat, and smile with complete comfort and confidence again.
Full Mouth Reconstruction
After enough teeth go missing, it can start to affect the entire bite. Rather than addressing each issue individually, a full mouth reconstruction lets us combine multiple procedures into a single, streamlined treatment plan. This lets patients get everything they need in a minimal number of appointments while restoring their health, function, and appearance at the same time.

page.content:
Dental Implants Houston
A Lasting Solution for Missing Teeth
The best things stand the test of time. That’s true for New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston (which has been serving Houston since 1981), and it’s true for dental implants. On top of looking and feeling just like real teeth, they’ve also been shown to last for 25 years and even a lifetime. If you’re ready to get a permanent solution for your tooth loss, book your consultation with us today to get started.
Why Choose New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston for Dental Implants?
Dental Implants Placed & Restored In-House
Kind, Friendly, & Experienced Dental Team
High-Quality & Budget-Friendly
What are Dental Implants?
Basically, a dental implant is a prosthetic tooth root that is surgically placed into the jawbone. It’s made of a strong and durable material like titanium or ceramic, and it will naturally bond with the surrounding bone. This makes it exceptionally sturdy, making it the perfect foundation for a new crown, bridge, or denture. 
The 4-Step Dental Implant Process
Consultation: You’ll sit down with Dr. Jetton, discuss your goals, and determine if dental implants are the right fit for you.
Surgery: Dr. Jetton can take care of the surgical placement of your implants himself, letting you get everything you need in the same hometown office.
Healing: While your mouth heals over the next three to six months, your implants will meld with your jawbone, making them incredibly stable and strong.
Restoration: The big day has arrived! Dr. Jetton will attach your new teeth to your implants, make a few final checks, and that’s it!
Benefits of Dental Implants
Durability: Traditional bridges and dentures last about 5-10 years on average, while dental implants have an impressive 25+ year lifespan.
Bite Strength: With implants, patients recover much more of their original bite strength compared to regular bridges and dentures (Around 70% compared to 20%).
Natural-Looking: Implants don’t have metal or acrylic attachments—they sit within your gums and jawbone just like real teeth.
Bone Loss Protection: Because implants stimulate your jawbone with every bite, they actively stop the bone loss that often develops after tooth loss.

page.title: Invisalign® Houston, TX | New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston
page.description: Straighten your smile with discreet, comfortable Invisalign aligners in Houston at New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston.
page.content:
Invisalign® Houston
The Easy Way to Straighten Teeth
Your teeth are an essential part of all your day-to-day life—you use them to eat your favorite foods, talk with your friends, and smile. If your teeth aren’t lined up just right, eating, talking, and smiling are more difficult.
To give you the perfect bite, we are proud to offer Invisalign clear aligners in Houston. These nearly invisible trays fit snugly over your teeth and work over a series of weeks to straighten them. Dr. Jetton has helped hundreds of patients with this approach, and he’s eager to do the same for you. To get started, book your consultation today.
Why Choose New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston for Invisalign®?
Dr. Jetton is a Diamond+ Invisalign Provider
Treatment Planned Using the Latest Technology
Budget-Friendly Payment Options
How Does Invisalign® Work?
Invisalign treatment uses a series of clear aligners that are custom-crafted to fit your mouth to more comfortably straighten teeth. Worn every day, the aligners gradually shift your teeth into the optimal position. Our patients have found them to be the ideal alternative to traditional braces!
Many people opt for Invisalign clear aligners instead of braces because they get all of the same benefits of straight teeth without having to wear uncomfortable—and highly noticeable—metal braces. Because Invisalign aligners are removable, you can take them out to clean, instead of working around the brackets of braces when you brush and floss.
The Invisalign Process
If you’ve been dreaming of a straighter smile, the first thing that you want to do is take advantage of our FREE consultation. You might find that Invisalign clear aligners are the most appealing solution. When you come into our office, we will analyze your smile and show you a digital representation of what it will look like post-treatment.
We will discuss with you the best options for moving forward, and if you decide you’d like to receive the Invisalign treatment, we will follow the following steps:
Impressions: Before we can make any improvements to your smile, we need to know where your teeth are. Your smile is unique, and we want to make aligners that are designed specifically for you.
3D Imaging: The technology that we use allows you to see the completed version of your smile so that you can envision the results of the Invisalign invisible braces.
Designing Aligners: We will take the information that we have gathered and create your Invisalign trays. When you receive the aligners, you will start wearing them every day, for at least 20–22 hours a day.
Wearing Your Aligners: When your teeth have moved to completely fit a set of aligners (with no more pressure), you will start wearing the next set of aligners that will continue to adjust your teeth. As long as you wear the aligners correctly, you should change aligners about every 1–2 weeks.
Who Invisalign® Can Help
We are committed to transforming as many smiles as we can with Invisalign invisible braces. The Invisalign formula has been perfected for years, making it a great fit for teens and adults alike! At New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston, we offer a free consultation to show you what Invisalign can do for you. Invisalign is generally recommended to patients who suffer from minor to moderate cases of:
Overbite
Overcrowding
Underbite
Smile gaps
Benefits of Invisalign®
The Invisalign system features a series of clear, smooth, plastic aligners that simply slip over your teeth and begin progressively straightening your smile. One of the most notable features of this system is the aligner’s appearance being virtually invisible! Instead of bulky metal brackets and wires, you can straighten your smile with sleek, transparent, comfortable material. More reasons to love Invisalign include:
Easier brushing & flossing
No food restrictions
Faster treatment time
Proven incredible results
What’s the Harm in Using Mail-Order Aligners?
Straight teeth don’t just help you look better; they also set your oral health for future success. If you want the benefits of aligned teeth, the cheapest option can’t be counted on for the best results.
Many companies recognize this and have sought to exploit this opportunity to their advantage. There are now hundreds of products available on the market that can be harmful to your health. However, what many people don’t realize is that when you purchase an oral product not recommended by a dentist, it can be dangerous and even cause permanent damage!
Read More
The Dangers of Mail-Order Aligners
Mail-order aligners may look convenient due to their cost, but they can do a lot more harm than good. Consider the fact that thousands of customers have filed complaints with the Better Business Bureau. Here are the reasons why consumers need to be careful:
No checkups or consultations: Not everyone meets the conditions needed for orthodontic treatment with aligners, but the mail-order companies won’t assess your situation beforehand. Certain things like severe overbites, impacted teeth, or severely crowded teeth, may require different solutions. Getting a professional consultation prior to ordering aligners is important for your oral health.
The impressions can be faulty or inaccurate: Invisalign aligners are created using highly accurate digital impressions of your teeth done by a dentist. Mail-order companies typically require you to take your own teeth impressions with dental putty. This is a tricky process that is very easy to make mistakes with. Planning your treatment around incorrect impressions to start with can make your alignment problem worse.
No follow-up appointments: All mouths are unique and require an individual treatment plan. When you pay for Invisalign aligners, your treatment includes monitored care from dental professionals. You’ll come in for periodic assessments so that we can make sure that your treatment is progressing according to schedule and make adjustments if needed. The same thing cannot be said about using mail-order aligners.
Though the mail-order option may seem appealing because of the cost and seeming convenience of doing it yourself, the risk it poses to your teeth is not worth it. With all of the problems mentioned above, there’s no guarantee that you’re getting the right treatment, and there’s a chance that you’ll end up paying more long-term if you damage your teeth.
Professional Care from a Dentist You Trust
When it comes to your orthodontic care, you want to know you’re getting the best service for the best price. Don’t sacrifice your teeth in favor of your wallet.
When you pay for an Invisalign treatment from a certified dentist, you aren’t just buying the technology; you are purchasing the expertise and supervision that comes with it. Orthodontics is a medical specialty, meaning that it’s critical that the right people are protecting the smile you’ve worked hard for.
Dr. Jetton is trained to ensure that you get the quality patient care you expect while aligning your teeth. This is a careful process that requires professional administration.
If you need your car fixed, you don’t trust just anyone to fix it; you would take it to a mechanic. This is why the American Dental Association (ADA) says that anyone who is looking to undergo orthodontic treatment should hire a trained dental professional. Here at New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston, you’ll get the professional dental treatment you need to get the straight smile you’ll love.
A Safe & Proven Method For Straightening Teeth
At New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston, we use Invisalign clear aligners because they are the most trusted technology for aligning patients’ teeth. The Invisalign system is safe, practical, and has the proper science to back it up. We offer a free assessment when you come into our office so that we can decide together if Invisalign is the right solution for your situation.

Sedation Dentist Houston
Less Stress, More Smiles
Every year, dental anxiety stops millions of people from getting the care they need. If you’re nervous about the dentist, we completely understand, and we’re ready to help. Sedation dentistry in Houston is a safe, proven way to help you feel calm in the treatment chair, whether you need a simple checkup or something more involved. You don’t need to worry about your smile anymore—we got you!
Why Choose New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston for Sedation Dentistry?
Choice of Sedation Options
Kind, Skilled, & Empathetic Dental Team
Trusted by Houston Since 1981
Nitrous Oxide Sedation
You’ve probably heard of nitrous oxide being called “laughing gas” before. While it doesn’t usually give patients the giggles, a few deep breaths do create feelings of warmth, even euphoria. It comes on quickly and goes away just as fast once the visit is over, with no lasting effects! That means you get right back to your day without delay.
Oral Conscious Sedation
On paper, oral conscious sedation sounds too good to be true. “You mean I can take a pill to make my dental nerves go away?” Yes! We’ll prescribe you medication and time it so that by the time you’re in the chair, you’re already fully relaxed. Because of its strength, be sure to have a trusted person drive you to and from your appointment.
IV Dental Sedation
IV sedation can help people with the most extreme dental anxiety. It’s also great for those who need more complex treatments or who want to complete multiple procedures in a single sitting to save time. The medication is administered directly into the bloodstream, helping a patient become relaxed almost immediately. With it, your appointment will fly by and be over before you know it.

Root Canal Treatment Houston
A Solution for Toothaches
It’s hard to focus on anything else when you have a toothache. But with root canal treatment, we can put a stop to your pain and save your tooth. All you need to do is reach out to New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston, and we’ll schedule you for an appointment as soon as possible. For over 45 years, we’ve helped Houston get the relief they need without waiting, so call today.
Why Choose New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston for Root Canal Treatment?
Same-Day Emergency Dental Appointments Available
Kind, Empathetic, & Experienced Dental Team
Multiple Sedation Options to Help with Anxiety
What Happens During a Root Canal?
Despite what you may have seen in movies or on TV, a root canal is a fairly straightforward and comfortable process.
After we’ve numbed your problem tooth, we make a small hole in the enamel. Through this, we remove the infected tissue (the source of the pain), sanitize, and fill the area. We then place a crown to restore strength to the tooth, and that’s it! Most patients say it feels similar to getting a small filling, which is to say it’s not that big of a deal.

When are Tooth Extractions Necessary?
When a tooth has severe decay or physical trauma to the point that it can’t be fixed with a filling or crown.
A tooth has been cracked beneath the gum line.
Advanced gum disease has made the tooth unstable.
More room is needed in the mouth for a denture or orthodontics.
The tooth is impacted, or stuck (often happens with wisdom teeth).

page.content:
Wisdom Tooth Extraction Houston
A Smooth Rite of Passage
New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston has been serving local families for over 45 years, which means we’ve helped a lot of adults and teens with wisdom teeth. Dr. Jetton knows how to make wisdom tooth extractions in Houston convenient and comfortable, ensuring an easy experience in the chair and during recovery. Whether for yourself or your child, we’re ready to provide everything you need without a referral—reach out today to book your appointment.
Why Choose New Teeth Dental Solutions - Houston for Wisdom Tooth Extraction?
Sedation Options Available for Nervous Patients
Friendly, Kind, & Skilled Dental Team
Ready to Help Both Teens & Adults
Why Do Wisdom Teeth Need to Be Removed?
Wisdom teeth are the third (and last) set of permanent molars to appear, but they aren’t particularly useful in today’s world. By the time they grow in, your mouth is already overcrowded. This increases the likelihood that wisdom teeth will grow in crooked, cause spacing issues, or shift the position of your other teeth.
To prevent them from causing harm to your other teeth and to fix impacted wisdom teeth, which can be painful, extraction is often necessary in order to ensure your oral health and the proper functioning of your teeth.
When Do Wisdom Teeth Need to Be Removed?
The only way to know if your wisdom teeth will be a problem is if you come to an appointment with us. When you come into our office, we will take an X-ray of your mouth so that we have a better understanding of what is happening with your teeth. If we see any of the following, it will be an indication that you need to get your wisdom teeth removed:
Overcrowding: As mentioned above, only a certain number of teeth can fit comfortably in your mouth at the same time. When wisdom teeth grow in, there is usually not enough space. As a result, the rest of your teeth will occupy the same area and become uncomfortably crowded.
Bite Issues: When your teeth run out of room, they begin to shift, which leads to a misaligned bite. If left untreated, an improper bite can create headaches that are caused by pressure and unnecessary strain from your other teeth overcompensating.
Impacted Teeth: An impacted tooth is a tooth that cannot grow out of the gums; without room to grow, the tooth buckles down in the gums. Because they are trying to erupt from the gums but are blocked, they can cause painful pressure in your gums and jaw.
Now that we’ve identified factors that could require you to have your wisdom teeth removed, we’ll give you a look at the removal process so that you’ll know what to expect on the day of the procedure.
The Wisdom Tooth Extraction Process
After determining that your wisdom teeth need to be removed, we will schedule an appointment where you come into our office for an extraction. You’ve probably heard stories about how difficult recovery can be, and that’s why we want to make sure you’re prepared for the procedure and what recovery entails.
Sedation: Our primary concern (in addition to providing you with amazing results, of course!) is your comfort as a patient. Before beginning the procedure, we will numb your mouth so you feel as little as possible.
Extraction: We will then gently remove your wisdom tooth with the use of our expert equipment. The procedure is relatively quick and usually takes less than an hour in total to complete.
Education: Our team will show you how to properly care for your teeth after the extraction. We will instruct you on how to clean the location of the tooth so it heals properly, and give you guidelines on the appropriate food to eat so that the area won’t become infected.
Recovery: Recovering from any surgery is no fun. To have a quick and relatively easy recovery, follow our guidelines. You will be able to avoid developing dry socket, gum pain, infection, and return to your normal activities and the food that you love soon!

Your Invisalign dentist examines your scan and creates a mock-up of your personal treatment plan.
We’ll show you a digital rendering of what your smile can look like post-treatment.

Our goal for your consultation is that when you leave, you feel educated and excited about all of the possibilities that Invisalign clear aligners can offer you. By the time you get home, you’ll have a much better sense of what Invisalign invisible braces can do for you.
Quality Patient Education

During your visit, please ask questions. We want to make sure you’re getting the care you need and expect. Each smile is different, and we know that there are specific concerns that you want to address. Don’t hesitate to bring them up so we can treat you better.
